title: The Role of Uncertainty in Assessing the Fairness of Machine Learning Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.07959v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Machine learning models are widely used in clinical applications, social media, law enforcement and critical infrastructure. Verifying whether their outputs are biased against disadvantaged groups or individuals is crucial to ensuring they are fair and allowing their use in such settings. A rigorous risk assessment of possible fairness violations requires quantifying the uncertainty associated with selecting and estimating such models. Yet, this is rarely done in the literature, which focuses on identifying a single model with a suitable trade-off between predictive accuracy and fairness. In this paper, we move beyond point estimation and discuss frequentist and Bayesian approaches to uncertainty quantification for fair machine learning, with practical examples and implications for simulated and real data.

translated_title: 不确定性在评估机器学习模型公平性中的作用
translated_abstract: 机器学习模型被广泛应用于临床医疗、社交媒体、执法部门和关键基础设施等领域。验证这些模型的输出是否对弱势群体或个人存在偏见，对于确保其公平性并允许其在此类场景中使用至关重要。对可能存在的公平性问题进行严格的风险评估，需要量化与模型选择和估计相关的不确定性。然而，现有文献很少做到这一点，它们大多集中于寻找一个在预测准确性和公平性之间达到合适权衡的单一模型。在本文中，我们超越了点估计的范畴，探讨了公平机器学习中不确定性量化的频率学派和贝叶斯方法，并结合模拟数据和真实数据的实际示例与应用影响加以说明。
tldr: 该论文超越了传统点估计方法，提出用频率学派和贝叶斯方法量化公平机器学习中的不确定性，从而对模型可能存在的偏见进行更严格的风险评估。
en_tdlr: This paper moves beyond point estimation by proposing frequentist and Bayesian approaches for uncertainty quantification in fair machine learning, enabling more rigorous risk assessment of potential fairness violations.
